Distribution.text: Engine P&A segment's net sales increased in the third quarter of 2025 compared to the third quarter of 2024, due to benefits from late-season weather in many regions and market share gains in our distribution business.

Engine Parts and Accessories.text: Net sales increased 7% during the third quarter of 2025 when compared with the third quarter of 2024, reflecting strong orders from OEMs and dealers, steady boating participation driving Engine Parts and Accessories (Engine P&A) and other aftermarket business strength and pricing action taken in recent periods. The Propulsion segment delivered significant sales growth, with revenues in each of its three business lines: outboard; sterndrive; and controls, rigging, and propellers up over the prior year as OEM order strength continued to later into the boating season. Our Engine P&A segment had another strong quarter, as healthy boater participation led to sales improvement compared to the prior year. Navico Group reported modest sales growth over the prior year quarter and operating margin was negatively affected by impairment charges. Refer to Note 8 - Goodwill and Other Intangibles in the Notes to Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements for further information on impairments. Growth was led by strong performance in the marine electronics portfolio as we start to see the benefits of investments in new products and technology. Finally, our Boat segment revenue grew over prior year and operating margin was consistent with prior year as our premium brands continued to perform well, and our aluminum boat businesses delivered a very strong quarter.

Electronics.text: Navico Group segment's net sales increased in the third quarter of 2025 compared to the third quarter of 2024, led by growth in its electronics portfolio.

intro.text: References to "we," "us," "our," the "Company," "Brunswick," and "Brunswick Corporation" refer to Brunswick Corporation and its consolidated subsidiaries unless the context specifically states or implies otherwise. Brunswick Corporation is a global leader in marine recreation, delivering innovation that transforms experiences on the water and beyond. Our unique, technology-driven solutions are informed and inspired by deep consumer insights and powered by our belief that “Next Never Rests."™ We design, manufacture, and market recreational marine products, including leading marine propulsion products and boats, as well as parts and accessories for the marine and RV markets, and we operate the world's largest boat club.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Business Acceleration businesses accounted for 14 percent of B oat seg ment net sales in 2025.

The Boat segment procures substantially all of its engines from Brunswick's Propulsion segment, and boats typically incorporate a significant volume of parts and accessories supplied by the Engine P&A and Navico Group segments.
Our customers rely on clean air and water to enjoy our products and services.

We may rely on short-term capital markets to meet our working capital requirements, fund capital expenditures or pay dividends, and we maintain short-term borrowing facilities that can be used to meet these capital requirements.
We rely on third parties to supply raw materials used in the manufacturing process, including oil, aluminum, copper, steel, and resins, as well as product parts and components.

In addition, some components used in our manufacturing processes, including certain engine components, furniture, upholstery, and boat windshields, are available from a sole supplier or a limited number of suppliers.
It may be difficult to find a replacement supplier for a limited or sole source raw material, part, or component without significant delay or on commercially reasonable terms.

These risks are exacerbated in the case of single-source suppliers, and the exclusive supplier of a key component could potentially exert significant bargaining power over price, quality, warranty claims, or other terms.
Additionally, if such an event occurs at or near our business locations, manufacturing facilities, or key supplier facilities, business operations and/or operating systems could be interrupted.
Our ability to remain competitive depends on successfully introducing new products, experiences, and services that meet customer expectations.
We rely on third-party dealers and distributors to sell most of our products.
We depend on these systems for commercial transactions, customer interactions, manufacturing, branding, employee tracking, and other applications.
We rely on third parties for computing, storage, processing, and similar services.

We collect, store, process, share, and use personal information, and rely on third parties that are not directly under our control to do so as well, which subjects us to legal obligations, laws and regulations related to security and privacy, and any actual or perceived failure to meet those obligations could harm our business.

We are subject to various data protection and privacy laws and regulations in the countries where we operate because we collect, store, process, share, and use personal information, and we rely on third parties that are not directly under our control to do so as well.
Our success depends upon the continued strength of our brands.

We rely on a combination of patents, trademark, copyright, and trade secret laws; employee and third-party non-disclosure agreements; and other contracts to establish and protect our technology and other intellectual property rights.
We actively engage with key vendors, industry participants, and law enforcement communities as part of our continuing efforts to evaluate and improve our program.
Purchases from TMC were $ 99.6 million, $ 79.6 million and $ 80.2 million in 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively.

s.t: During the year ended December 31, 2023, the Company recorded an impairment charge of $ 19.2 million due to a decline in the fair value of its investment in TN-BC Holdings LLC (the Joint Venture), as a result of a reduction in value of certain of the Joint Venture's underlying investments.

The Company has a 50 percent interest in TN-BC Holdings LLC (the Joint Venture), which is a joint venture accounted for as an equity method investment, between the Company and TechNexus Holdings LLC formed in 2017.
